plan.title: Mouse liver HFD vs chow DE + Hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: Twelve mouse liver samples (6 high-fat diet vs 6 chow, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes) are analyzed for differential expression and pathway change. Sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median and is flagged for inspection, not silently dropped, per the low-depth-sample rule: it is kept through QC, its position on PCA and the sample-distance heatmap and its detected-gene count are reported, and it is removed only if that inspection gives a concrete reason (e.g. it is a clear outlier off its group, not just low depth, since DESeq2 size factors already down-weight depth differences). Track 1 runs standard DESeq2 QC -> minimal pre-filter -> median-of-ratios normalization -> Wald test with an explicit condition reference level (chow as reference, contrast HFD vs chow) -> apeglm LFC shrinkage -> BH-adjusted results at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, plus an edgeR quasi-likelihood fit on the same design as a robustness cross-check (report the intersection as the high-confidence gene set). Track 2 takes the DESeq2 Wald statistic for every tested gene and runs fgsea preranked GSEA against the MSigDB mouse Hallmark gene sets (15-500 member window, BH-adjusted, redundancy collapsed, leading-edge genes reported) to answer which hallmark pathways differ between HFD and chow liver. A final report step consolidates DE results, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, QC diagnostics (including the sample_01 disposition), and the Hallmark GSEA table with leading-edge genes and full reproducibility metadata.

steps.method: vst(blind) PCA, sample distances, library size QC
keep genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (smallest group size)
~condition, explicit reference level = chow/control, contrast = condition HFD vs chow
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (second method for robustness)
fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald stat, MSigDB mouse Hallmark gene sets
DE + enrichment report with diagnostics, overlap of DESeq2/edgeR, leading edge genes
